header.running_head: Enduring Injuries and Illness when Inviting People Towards Allaah

blocks.text: The Story of Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA) and his Martyrdom During the Battle of Uhud

Several elders of the Banu Salma tribe have reported that Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA) was badly crippled while his four sons were like lions and participated in every battle by the side Rasulullaah ﷺ. When the Battle of Uhud took place, his sons tried to prevent him from participating saying, "Allaah has excused you." He then approached Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "My sons want to stop me from leaving with you to participate in this battle. By Allaah! I wish to walk in Jannah with my paralysis." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Allaah has excused you. Jihaad is not compulsory for you." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to his sons, "You need not prevent him (from participating) because Allaah may perhaps grant him the high rank of martyrdom." Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA) then left with Rasulullaah ﷺ and was martyred during the Battle of Uhud.[^1]

Hadhrat Abu Qataadah (RA) who participated in the Battle of Uhud says that Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA) who was crippled once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! If I fight in the path of Allaah and am killed, will I walk with a healthy leg in Jannah?" "Certainly," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. Subsequently, the Kuffaar martyred Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA), his nephew and their slave during the Battle of Uhud. When Rasulullaah ﷺ passed by (the corpse of) Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA), he said, "I can see him walking in Jannah with a healthy leg." Rasulullaah ﷺ then instructed that Hadhrat Amr bin Jamooh (RA), his nephew and slave should be buried in one grave.[^2]
The Story of Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA)

Hadhrat Yahya bin Abdul Hameed narrates from his grandfather that an arrow struck Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA) during either the Battle of Uhud or the Battle of Hunayn[^3]. He then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked him to remove the arrow. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Raafi! If you want, I could remove the shaft together with arrowhead. Otherwise, I could remove only the shaft without arrowhead and testify on the Day of Qiyaamah that you are a martyr." Hadhrat Raafi (RA) said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Remove the shaft without the arrowhead and testify for me on the Day of Qiyaamah that I am a martyr." Rasulullaah ﷺ did this. Hadhrat Raafi (RA) lived until the period when Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) was Khalifah, when the wound reopened and he passed away after Asr.

Such is the report according to this narration. However, the correct version of the story according to Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya is that Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA) passed away after the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA). Isaaba (Vol.1 Pg.496) states that a period elapsed between the time his wound reopened and the time that he passed away.[^4] Several such Ahadeeth shall Insha Allaah be quoted in the chapter discussing patience.
Ibn Is'haaq as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.4 Pg.37).
Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.315) has commented on the chain of narrators. Bayhaqi (Vol.9 Pg.24) has also reported the narration.
One of narrators Amr bin Marzooq is unsure which battle it was.
Bayhaqi. The narration is also reported by Baawardi, Ibn Mandah and Tabraani as quoted in Isaaba (Vol.4 Pg.474) as well as Ibn Shaaheen as quoted in Isaaba (Vol.1 Pg.496).
